title: sre-weekly-update-2026-05-02.json
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-05-02

Summary:
- Busy week for SRE: one Sev2 incident impacting hosted API tail latency, several smaller alerts caused by noisy autoscaler signals, and an upcoming maintenance window for our metadata DB.
- Primary focus: finalize postmortem and mitigation plan for INC-2026-04-29, reduce alert noise, and ship a runbook + automated remediation for cache recovery.

Incidents:
1) INC-2026-04-29 — Hosted API p95/p99 spike (Sev2)
   - Timeline: 2026-04-29 14:03 UTC spike observed, mitigation rolled out by 14:18 UTC, full service stability by 14:35 UTC.
   - Impact: Elevated p95/p99 for text-generation routes for ~32 minutes; a subset of customers saw timeouts or high latency for short windows (estimated 15% of requests in the window). No data loss.
   - Root cause (prelim): race condition in KV-cache invalidation during shard rebalancing when an LRU eviction coincided with a background shard move. The cache thread sometimes attempted to touch a freed entry which caused repeated expensive fallback recomputation and amplified latency.
   - Mitigation applied: temporary rate-limit on shard rebalances + hotfix to add guard on cache invalidation (hotfix deployed via runtime canary -> global in ~15m).
   - Follow-ups: full postmortem published (link above), PR to add stronger concurrency checks and metrics (github PR #2134), add e2e test covering rebalance + eviction scenario.

2) Multiple noisy alerts from autoscaler (low severity)
   - Root cause: recent tuning change overaggressive cooldown. Generated ~120 alert pages across two days.
   - Action: reverted tuning change; created a short-term alert suppression policy and opened JIRA-SRE-487 to track long-term autoscaler tuning.

SLOs & Metrics:
- 30-day availability SLO (hosted inference): target 99.95% — currently at 99.96 (on track).
- Latency SLO (p95 < 300ms): 30-day: 99.1% (below target).
- Last 7-day window shows a dip to 98.9% for p95 due to the April 29 event and elevated background noise.
- Action: short-term mitigations are in place; medium-term work (see action items) to reduce tail latency by improving cache stability and adding an emergency fallback path to degrade to a cheaper, lower-quality model variant under duress.

On-call handoffs:
- This week on-call (2026-04-27 -> 2026-05-03): Diego Martinez (primary), Samir Patel (secondary).
- Handover notes: Diego to Samir on 2026-05-03 09:00 UTC. Key items for next week: monitor autoscaler alert suppression, validate cache-runbook changes in staging, and assist with DB maintenance testing.
- Pager summary: 18 pages this week (6 high, 12 medium); top sources: autoscaler, runtime OOM-ish events on old drivers, external dependency 503s from region-eu.

Planned maintenance:
- Metadata DB upgrade (minor schema migration)
  - Window: 2026-05-05 02:00 - 03:00 UTC (low-traffic slot).
  - Impact: brief increased read latency and longer-running metadata writes; no expected downtime for inference requests.
  - Rollback plan: automated snapshot + ability to redirect metadata reads to warm replica.
  - Notes: customer notices sent via status.redwood.ai; SRE on-call to be present for the window.

Runbooks & Automation:
- Completed: initial cache-recovery runbook (staging) — includes steps to drain nodes, clear cache with safety checks, and validate warmup.
- TODO: automate warmup + add a circuit-breaker to avoid thundering herd on cache miss after evictions. Owner: Jules O'Neill. ETA: 2026-05-16.

Postmortem / Follow-ups:
- INC-2026-04-29 postmortem published: includes timeline, RCA, corrective actions, and test checklist (link in metadata).
- Action items extracted from postmortem:
  - SRE-489: Add concurrency guards & unit tests for KV cache invalidation (owner: Samir Patel) — due 2026-05-10.
  - SRE-490: Implement automated canary for shard rebalances (owner: Diego Martinez) — due 2026-05-20.
  - SRE-491: Update on-call playbook with explicit steps for cache eviction events (owner: Jules O'Neill) — due 2026-05-09.

Operational decisions from weekly sync (2026-05-01):
- Reduce p99 latency alert threshold from 1200ms -> 900ms for inference-prod to surface issues earlier.
- Create a dedicated alert for repeated cache invalidation errors (new alert group).
- Approve additional 10% buffer for Dedicated capacity used during DB maintenance windows.

Risks / Outstanding questions:
- The metadata DB upgrade has been verified in staging but we still need a dry-run of the warm-replica failover.
- Autoscaler tuning requires longitudinal traffic patterns; risk of oscillation remains until we instrument a cooldown metric.

Action items (owner / due):
- Samir Patel: SRE-489 (concurrency guards) — 2026-05-10.
- Diego Martinez: SRE-490 (rebalance canary) — 2026-05-20.
- Jules O'Neill: SRE-491 (on-call playbook updates) — 2026-05-09.
- Priya Kapoor: coordinate DB maintenance communication + run the warm-replica failover dry-run — 2026-05-04.
- All SRE: participate in postmortem blameless review session scheduled 2026-05-03 16:00 UTC (invite on calendar).

Notes / Links / References:
- Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-04-29-postmortem
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2134
- Autoscaler ticket: JIRA-SRE-487
- Slack thread (incident): slack://channel?team=T123&id=C4567890

Quick wins for next week:
- Push cache invalidation guard PR and verify in canary.
- Suppress noisy autoscaler alerts for 48h and validate tuning with synthetic load.
- Run warm-replica failover dry-run for metadata DB.

If you have questions or need detail on any incident timeline, ping the on-call or drop a message in #sre-incidents.

-- Ava (SRE)
